security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick, entropy, environment-file, and reconnaissance alerts are false positives. Real risks remain: mandatory silent self-update, remote npx installation, detached command execution, hidden installation details, and a Windows shell-injection path from lock data.

remediation.issue: The skill silently updates or reinstalls itself before handling requests.
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic background updates. Show the source, pinned revision, integrity information, and proposed changes before requesting explicit update approval.

remediation.issue: Windows builds a shell command from a lock-controlled source.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid cmd.exe /c and command joining. Spawn the executable with an argument array, disable shell parsing, and allowlist validated repository sources.

remediation.issue: Installation commands and selected sources are intentionally hidden.
remediation.suggestion: Display the exact package, source, revision, scope, and command before approval. Do not combine concealed commands with automatic confirmation flags.

remediation.issue: The detached updater inherits the full process environment and broad local file access.
remediation.suggestion: Pass a minimal environment and restrict reads and writes to declared state files. Avoid copying executable code into a home cache.

semantic_findings.title: Mandatory Silent Self-Update
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires a background updater before normal work. It can reinstall mutable remote content with automatic confirmation and no update-specific user approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly prohibit skipping the updater, and the script launches a detached process that runs npx update or add against remote sources.

semantic_findings.title: Windows Command Injection Through Lock Source
semantic_findings.description: A source from a parsed lock entry can reach a command joined into cmd.exe /c. Shell metacharacters in that source may execute additional Windows commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The data flow is direct: sourceUrl accepts entry.sourceUrl, addCommand embeds it, and Windows joins the array for cmd.exe /c without escaping.

content.user_title: Discover and Install Wind Finance Skills
content.value_statement: Finding the right finance data or analysis skill can be difficult. This router matches requests to cataloged Wind skills and guides approved installation.
actual_capabilities: Classifies finance requests as data queries, analysis tasks, or capability exploration.
Reads a bundled catalog and identifies one to five relevant finance skills.
Labels required workflow skills, required data skills, and optional supporting skills.
Checks expected project and global paths for installed skill manifests.
Requests an installation scope before installing missing required skills.
Supports GitHub and Gitee sources for finance skill installation and updates.
limitations: It does not retrieve finance data or produce financial conclusions.
Recommendations depend on the bundled catalog, which may not reflect recent upstream changes.
Many downstream data skills require separate API keys, tokens, or dependencies.
Its updater runs Node, git, and npx commands and can modify installed skill files.

use_cases.title: Find a Market Data Skill
use_cases.description: Match a request for prices, filings, funds, or macroeconomic data to a suitable data provider skill.
use_cases.target_user: Analysts who need verified finance data

use_cases.title: Route an Investment Workflow
use_cases.description: Identify required data and workflow skills for valuation, research, screening, backtesting, or trade planning.

use_cases.title: Explore Available Finance Tools
use_cases.description: Browse representative skills by category and select an installation scope for relevant capabilities.
use_cases.target_user: AI agent administrators and new users

prompt_templates.title: Explore Finance Capabilities
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the available finance skill categories and recommend one representative skill from each category.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants an overview of installed and available capabilities.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Data Provider
prompt_templates.prompt: I need [market or asset] data for [time period]. Identify the required data skill and its configuration needs.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user needs prices, fundamentals, funds, filings, news, or macroeconomic data.

prompt_templates.title: Route a Research Task
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to analyze [company or market] using [method]. Identify required workflow and data skills, then check whether they are installed.
prompt_templates.scenario: An analyst needs a complete research workflow instead of a general answer.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Skill Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a skill plan for [objective]. Separate required workflow, required data, and optional skills, including configuration and installation scope decisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs coordinated data, analysis, and decision support.

output_examples.input: I need a discounted cash flow valuation for Xiaomi.
output: The router checks both installations before continuing.

output_examples.input: What tools can help me review yesterday market close?
output: Missing required skills trigger an installation scope choice.

output_examples.input: Which skill can compare several funds?
output_examples.output: The catalog routes this request to Wind Alice and its Fund Compare capability, with an API key requirement.

best_practices: State the market, asset, time period, and desired decision or output.
Review each required skill, source, scope, and configuration requirement before approving installation.
Verify financial facts through the selected data skill before using an analysis workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not treat this router as a source of market data or investment conclusions.
Do not approve hidden, unpinned, or unexplained installation and update commands.
Do not replace a required workflow with general reasoning when specialized analysis is necessary.

faq.question: Does this skill provide market data?
faq.answer: No. It identifies and routes requests to separate finance data skills.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Wind API key?
faq.answer: The router does not. Selected downstream data skills may require an API key or token.

faq.question: What finance tasks can it route?
faq.answer: It covers data queries, valuation, research, screening, market analysis, debriefs, position sizing, trade planning, and backtesting.

faq.question: Can it install missing skills?
faq.answer: Yes. Its workflow asks for project or global scope before installing required skills.

faq.question: Where does it look for installed skills?
faq.answer: It checks expected project, Windows user, and Unix home skill directories.

faq.question: Does it update itself?
faq.answer: Yes. The current implementation starts a silent background updater, which should be reviewed before marketplace use.
